chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “If a man intends to strike another man unjustly, and the man protects himself from him or wards him off from himself, and harm befalls him, then there is nothing against him.”

key_terms.دَفَعَهُ: he warded him off; he repelled the aggressor
key_terms.ضَرَرٌ: harm or injury resulting from the defensive act
key_terms.ظُلْمًا: unjustly; indicating wrongful aggression without right
key_terms.عَنْ نَفْسِهِ: from himself; in defense of his own person
key_terms.فَاتَّقَاهُ: he protected himself from him; he took defensive precaution against the attacker
key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is nothing against him; no liability or penalty is upon him

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if an unjust aggressor is harmed while being repelled in self-defense?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding self-defense against wrongful aggression. If a person repels an unjust attack in order to protect himself, and the aggressor is harmed as a result, no liability falls upon the one defending himself.
